prompt: Close-up of a whole chilled, family-style layered dessert for eight in a high-rimmed rectangular 15 x 25 cm baking dish, with one cut portion raised on a dessert server to reveal the layers. A generous amount of thick, smoothly whipped ivory mascarpone-quark cream, delicately freckled with cinnamon and fine orange zest, dominates two thinner layers of soft medium-brown gingerbread. The gingerbread hearts, pretzels and stars were split horizontally; their porous cut faces are patchily darkened and moistened by the sweetened coffee-amaretto drizzle while staying coherent. Between them sits a glossy, deep ruby-burgundy cherry compote; plump, softened dark-red cherries remain recognisable in lightly thickened juice. Inside the dish, the order is moist gingerbread, cream, cherry compote, cream, a second moist gingerbread layer, then the remaining cream spread flat. A fine, even dry dusting of cocoa covers the top in a matte cocoa-brown veil; the lifted piece shows all layers neatly set after chilling. The cocoa-covered dessert nearly fills the square frame, with the white ceramic dish edges cropped and a plain silver server as the only utensil. Photograph at a 65-degree angle in bright, soft natural daylight with crisp detail and true colours. A calm pale warm-wood table and a small edge of natural linen form a clean, unmarked background; the dessert looks cool, generously portioned and homemade.

visible_ingredients.name_de: Kirschkompott aus Kirschsaft und tiefgekühlten Kirschen
visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: 150 ml Kirschsaft (18.75 ml per serving), 10 g Vanillepuddingpulver (1.25 g), 40 g Rohrohrzucker (5 g), 0.5 TL Lebkuchengewürz (0.062 TL) and 350 g frozen cherries (43.75 g). The cherries provide most of the middle fruit layer's volume; the juice becomes their thickened coating, while pudding powder, sugar and spice are incorporated into that sauce.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: A glossy, deep ruby-red to burgundy compote. The briefly reheated frozen cherries are softened and slightly wrinkled but remain recognisable rather than puréed. The cooled juice lightly thickens and clings to them, making a spoonable, moist layer without becoming a firm jelly.

visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: 300 g total, 37.5 g per serving, split and divided equally between the bottom and upper biscuit layers. These two layers are visibly thinner and less voluminous than the cream made from 1 kg of mascarpone and quark.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: Soft, medium-brown baked spice biscuits with recognisable heart, pretzel and star outlines. Splitting them through the middle exposes a fine, porous brown crumb on broad, thin slices. Coffee creates irregular darker moist patches; after chilling, the slices are tender and coherent, not crisp or reduced to crumbs.

visible_ingredients.name_de: Mascarpone-Quark-Creme mit Amaretto, Zimt und Orangenabrieb
visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: 500 g mascarpone and 500 g quark (62.5 g of each per serving), mixed with 3 EL of the total 5 EL Amaretto, 80 g of the total 100 g Rohrzucker, 1 TL Zimtpulver (0.125 TL per serving) and 1 TL Orangenabrieb (0.125 TL per serving). This is the dominant component, used in three approximately equal layers.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: Thick, smooth and creamy after 3–5 minutes of whipping, with an ivory to pale cream colour and a spreadable, softly set surface我心里便宜吗. Very fine cinnamon speckling and tiny orange-zest flecks are visible on close inspection; the sugar and Amaretto are fully incorporated rather than separate textures.

visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: 100 ml strong coffee (12.5 ml per serving), the remaining 2 EL Amaretto and remaining 20 g Rohrzucker; the full recipe contains 5 EL Amaretto (0.625 EL per serving) and 100 g Rohrzucker (12.5 g per serving). Half the liquid is drizzled over each gingerbread layer, so it moistens the biscuit rather than forming a separate sauce.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: A dark-brown liquid during preparation, visible in the finished dessert only as uneven espresso-brown moist areas within the gingerbread. The biscuits retain their broad sliced forms, with no liquid pooling between the layers.

visible_ingredients.recipe_quantity_and_visual_proportion: 1 EL total, 0.125 EL per serving, used only as the final topping over the smooth upper cream layer.
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: A fine, dry, even dusting of matte cocoa brown, light enough to read as a powdery veil rather than a thick crust or sauce.

recipe_result: A chilled, firmly set layered dessert for 8 in a 15 x 25 cm baking dish, combining two coffee-moistened gingerbread layers, three whipped mascarpone-quark cream layers and a central cooked cherry compote, finished with cocoa and shown as the whole family-style dish with one cut portion being served.

final_plating_from_recipe: Following steps 2 and 4, the chilled high-rimmed baking dish is layered from the bottom with half the split gingerbread, half the coffee drizzle, one third of the cream, all the cooled cherry compote, another third of the cream, the remaining gingerbread, the remaining coffee drizzle and finally the last third of the cream, smoothed flat. After at least two hours covered in the refrigerator, step 6 adds the cocoa dusting and cuts the dessert into pieces. Keep the full baking dish in view and raise just one cut portion on a dessert server to expose the layer order. Step 6's additional cherry compote is optional; no separate accompaniment is required.

recipe_instructions.instruction: Für das Kirschkompott zunächst 4 EL Kirschsaft (für das Grundrezept von 8 Portionen) mithilfe eines Schneebesens mit dem Puddingpulver glattrühren. Übrigen Saft mit Zucker und Lebkuchengewürz in einem Topf aufkochen, Puddingpulver-Mischung einrühren und unter Rühren 1 Minute köcheln lassen. Tiefgekühlte Kirschen zugeben, noch einmal aufkochen, in eine Schüssel umfüllen und auskühlen lassen.
Eine Auflaufform mit hohem Rand (ca. 15 x 25 cm) kaltstellen. Lebkuchen mit einem Messer in der Mitte halbieren.
Mascarpone mit Quark, 3 EL Amaretto und 80 g Rohrzucker glattrühren. Zimt und Orangenabrieb zugeben und 3-5 Minuten cremig aufschlagen.

Restlichen Amaretto und Rohrzucker mit heißem Kaffee verrühren. Den Boden der Auflaufform mit der Hälfte der Lebkuchen-Scheiben auslegen und mit der Hälfte des Kaffees beträufeln. Ein Drittel der Creme darauf verteilen und glattstreichen. Ausgekühlte Kirschen darauf verteilen und mit einem weiteren Drittel der Creme bestreichen.

Restliche Lebkuchen auflegen, mit der Kaffeemischung beträufeln und die übrige Creme darauf glattstreichen. Tiramisu abgedeckt in den Kühlschrank stellen und mindestens 2 Stunden (am besten über Nacht) durchziehen lassen.
Tiramisu mit Kakao bestreuen, in Stücke schneiden und nach Wunsch mit einer Extraportion Kirschkompott servieren. Lass es dir schmecken!
